comment_content:
I don't agree with blaming data science schools for this. Good schools are
teaching enough of 'analysis using code'  (not programming). I understand that
people coming from programming background  tend to ask questions like coding a
bubble sort or anagram or Fibonacci series using recursion or traversing a
tree - I would say questions should depend on what data scientist does during
day to day operations. if you are a company deploying solutions on cloud with
decent exposure to software stack like web applications, data bases, front end
and back end and  you deal with billions of data points and 'efficiency' of
model execution is as much more imp than insights, then you can launch a
competition on code chef for data scientists On other hand if you are more a
statistical company working on client's drug tests results or an marketing
agency working an ad words responsiveness,  'analytical' skills are more
important and I will ask more about correlation or cross tab.  Every data
scientist role is not anagram to each other !!  (edited)
